sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner seeking the following relief:
"(a) Issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding and directing the respondents to pay Award/Compensation to the extent of four times of circle rate applicable to the Rural Areas for Acquisition of Land under Land Acquisition Act in the year 2014 of petitioner situated in Gata No.447 total area 0.417 hectare, acquired area 0.270 hectare, Village- Hardidally, Tehsil- Nautanwa, District- Maharajganj in pursuance of Government Order dated 19.03.2015."
Shakuntala Devi vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 12 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/176592894/
1

2. Submissions have been made that under the notification for Indo-Nepal Border Road Project,
lands of villagers in the districts of Siddharthnagar and Maharajganj were acquired and claims that four times the circle rate was to be awarded as compensation.

3. Pursuant to the said acquisition, the petitioner executed the sale deed dated 09.12.2014 in favour of the respondents and compensation, based on the said sale deed, amounting to Rs.5,01,400/- was paid to the petitioner.

4. Submissions have been made that the respondents have come out with a circular dated 19.03.2015 providing for higher rate of compensation for acquisition of lands and, therefore, the petitioner is entitled to seek further compensation from the respondents.

5. Pursuant to earlier orders, the respondents have produced the instructions in the matter wherein submissions have been made that once the sale deed was executed and execution stood completed on a particular rate, only on account of issuance of a subsequent circular dated 19.03.2015, the petitioner cannot claim for the compensation and, therefore, the petition deserves dismissal.

6. Learned counsel for the petitioner made submissions that the respondents are not justified in denying enhanced compensation to the petitioner only on account of the fact that the circular came to be issued later on and those land that have subsequently been purchased would be entitled to higher compensation and, therefore, the petition deserves to be accepted.

7. Learned Government Counsel reiterated the submissions that the transaction entered between the petitioner and the respondents cannot be revisited, based on each subsequent circular, which is issued only on account of the circumstances subsequent thereto and, therefore, the petition deserves dismissal.
8. We have considered submissions made by learned counsel for the parties and have perused the material available on record.
It is not in dispute that the sale deeds have already been executed by the petitioner on 09.12.2014 and compensation, as awarded to him vide cheque dated 09.12.2014,

The mere fact that subsequent circular has been issued providing for a higher compensation, which apparently pertains to the land, which was to be acquired in future i.e.,
after the notification has been issued, cannot be made applicable to the land, which already stands acquired prior to the issuance of the circular dated 19.03.2015 so as to reopen the concluded transactions.
9.
In that view of the matter, we are firmly of the opinion that the petitioner is not entitle to any relief.

(Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) (Arun Bhansali, C.J.)
